title: Understanding Linear Models
text: A linear model is one where the relationship between the dependent variable and the independent variables is linear with respect to the parameters (coefficients).

title: Identifying Linear Models
text: Consider whether the model can be expressed in the form $$y=\theta_1 x_1+\theta_2 x_2+...+\theta_n x_n$$, where thetas are the parameters.

hintAnswer: Yes, it is a linear model with respect to theta.
title: Example of a Linear Model
text: Is the model $$y=\theta_1 x_1+\theta_2 x_2$$ a linear model with respect to theta?
choices: Yes, it is a linear model with respect to theta.

hintAnswer: Yes, it is still a linear model with respect to theta because the parameters are not raised to any power.
title: Non-linear Model Example
text: Is the model $$y=\theta_1 {x_1}^2+\theta_2 x_2$$ a linear model with respect to theta?
choices: Yes, it is still a linear model with respect to theta because the parameters are not raised to any power.
